/cookies.title: Cookie policy — Sightwork, AI agency & consulting
/cookies.description: The cookies this site uses and how to switch them off.
p: This page explains the cookies used on the Sightwork website, what each one is for and how to switch them off. The list is short on purpose: we use only what keeps the site working and what tells us whether it helps people.
A cookie is a small text file a website saves in your browser. It lets the site remember something between pages or visits, such as a choice you made. Cookies cannot read other files on your device.

Analytics tells us things like how many people read the pricing page this month, how many started a booking and how many finished it, and whether a page is slow on phones. We use it to fix pages that confuse people. Analytics data is kept for fourteen months and then deleted.

Fonts and images load from our hosting provider. The calendar used to confirm a booking is provided by our booking tool, which may set its own essential cookies to hold the time slot you picked. A video, when a page has one, loads from the company that hosts it only after you press play. Their own policies apply to those cookies.
If you block every cookie the site still works: pages load and forms still send. Only small conveniences are lost, such as the booking form remembering the step you reached.
If your browser sends a Global Privacy Control signal, we treat it as a refusal of analytics cookies. No banner click is needed.
Essential cookies last for your visit, or up to twelve months for your cookie choice. Analytics cookies last up to fourteen months and then delete themselves.

When we add or remove a tool we update this page and the date at the top. Questions about cookies or your information: write to hello@sightwork.studio. Our privacy policy explains how we handle personal information in general.

/terms.title: Terms of service — Sightwork, AI agency & consulting
/terms.description: The terms for working with Sightwork.
p: These terms cover the use of the Sightwork website and the way we work with clients. They are written to be read. Every client engagement also has a signed statement of work, and where the two differ, the signed statement of work wins.

We work in fixed-scope engagements: an audit, a build or a run plan, each described in a statement of work with the deliverables, the timeline and the people involved. Work starts once the statement of work is signed by both sides and the first invoice is paid.

Agents run in your accounts and your cloud. When an engagement ends we hand over everything needed to run, change or move the agent without us. We keep the right to reuse general know-how and our own internal tools, which never contain your data.

To build an agent we need access to the systems it will work in and a person on your team who can answer questions within a working day. Delays on access or answers move the timeline by the same amount, without changing the fee.

You may not ask us to build an agent that deceives people, breaks the law, collects data without a lawful basis or makes decisions about people without a human able to review them. We may pause work that we reasonably believe crosses these lines and will tell you why.

Everything on this site describes how we work and what we have built. It is general information, not legal, financial or technical advice for your business. Case study numbers are real results for named clients and are not a promise of the same result for you.

We stand behind our work with a thirty-day fix period after launch. To the extent the law allows, our total liability under an engagement is limited to the fees paid for it, and neither side is liable for indirect or consequential losses. Nothing here limits liability that cannot be limited by law.
These terms and every engagement are governed by the laws of the State of California. Disputes belong to the state and federal courts in San Francisco County.
We may update these terms. The date at the top shows the latest version, and a signed statement of work keeps the terms it was signed under. Questions: hello@sightwork.studio.

/privacy.title: Privacy policy — Sightwork, AI agency & consulting
/privacy.description: How Sightwork collects, uses and protects personal data.
p: This policy explains what Sightwork collects when you visit this website, book a call, write to us or sign up for our letter, what we do with it and how you stay in control. It also covers the client data our agents work with, because that is the question we are asked most.

We use your details to prepare for the call, answer your message, send the proposal you asked for and, if you hire us, to run the engagement. We send the newsletter only to people who asked for it, and every issue has a one-click unsubscribe. We never sell personal information and we never use it for advertising on other websites.

When we build an agent for you, it runs in your accounts: your help desk, your CRM, your cloud. The data it reads and writes stays there, under a data processing agreement we sign before any access is granted.
We use model providers under business terms that do not allow training on your data, and we keep test sets and logs only for as long as the engagement needs them.

Your details are read by the strategists and engineers who work on your request. We use a small number of sub-processors to run the studio: email, calendar booking, file storage, analytics and the model providers named in your agreement. Each works under contract and may not use your information for its own purposes. The current list is available on request.

You can ask to see the information we hold about you, have it corrected or deleted, take a copy with you, or object to how we use it. California residents have the same rights under the CCPA, and we honor them for everyone. We answer every request within thirty days and never charge for it.

If we change this policy we post the new version here and change the date at the top. Questions, or a request about your information: write to hello@sightwork.studio. A person from the studio replies within one working day.
